fr.short: Version majeure du protocole http apportant multiplexing, compression d'en-têtes et push serveur pour améliorer les performances
fr.full:
**HTTP/2** est une révision majeure de HTTP apportant : multiplexing (plusieurs requêtes simultanées), compression d'en-têtes (HPACK), server push (envoi proactif ressources).

Différences : HTTP/1.1 = une requête/connexion, headers texte. HTTP/2 = multiplexing, headers binaires compressés, une connexion TCP.

Server Push : serveur envoie ressources (CSS, JS) avant demande client, réduit latence. Priorisation streams pour optimiser chargement. Supporté navigateurs modernes et serveurs web. Nécessite HTTPS. HTTP/3 utilise QUIC (UDP) vs TCP.

en.short: A major revision of the HTTP protocol that brings multiplexing, header compression and server push to improve performance
en.full:
**HTTP/2** is a major revision of HTTP that brings: multiplexing (multiple concurrent requests), header compression (HPACK) and server push (proactively sending resources).

Differences: HTTP/1.1 = one request per connection, text-based headers. HTTP/2 = multiplexing, compressed binary headers, a single TCP connection.

Server Push: the server sends resources (CSS, JS) before the client requests them, reducing latency. Stream prioritization optimizes loading. Supported by modern browsers and web servers. Requires HTTPS. HTTP/3 uses QUIC (UDP) instead of TCP.
